1389.3: Swayye in praise of the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. With a one-pointed mind meditating on the all-pervading Lord, the Giver of boons, the support of the Sants, ever manifest, I take his feet and enshrine them in my heart, and then I sing the virtues of the supreme Guru, Guru Nanak. ॥1॥
1389.4: I sing the virtues of the supreme Guru, the ocean of peace, the remover of sins, the pool of the Shabad. The deep, the steadfast and the oceans of wisdom sing of him; yogis and Jangams (wandering ascetics) fix their meditation on him. Indra and the others, and devotees like Prahlad, sing of him who has known the relish of the spirit. I, the poet Kal, sing the fair praise of Guru Nanak, who has enjoyed Raj and Jog. ॥2॥

Prahlad was the son of the demon king Harnakhash (Hiranyakashipu) and held to devotion to God through all his father's torments; in the Puranas, God took the form of Narasimha, the Man-Lion, and killed Harnakhash.

Kal, who also calls himself Kalsahar, is one of the Bhatts, the bards whose swayye are in Sri Guru Granth Sahib. Raj and Jog: sovereignty (raj) and union with God (jog) held together; the Guru rules like a king while remaining joined to God.
1389.5: Janak and the others, masters of yoga's way, sing of him who is full of the Lord's relish, possessed of every power. Sanak and his brothers, the Saadhs (the holy ones) and the Siddhas and others sing of him; the silent sages sing of him whom the deceiver (Maya) could not deceive. Dhom (the sage) and (Dhru,) whose realm is unshakable, sing the virtues of him who has known (the Lord's) relish through loving devotion. I, the poet Kal, sing the fair praise of Guru Nanak, who has enjoyed Raj and Jog. ॥3॥

Janak, king of Mithila and father of Sita, is remembered as a sage who stayed detached while he ruled. Dhom: a sage of the Mahabharata, the Pandavas' priest. He whose realm is unshakable: Dhru, the child prince who, slighted by his stepmother, gave himself to devotion and was given an unmoving place as the Pole Star.
1389.6: Kapil and the others, masters of yoga from of old, sing of him, the foremost incarnation of the Infinite (Lord). Parasram, (son) of Jamdagan, sings of him too, he from whom (Ram of) Raghu's (line) took the axe in his hand and his might. Udho, Akrur and Bidar sing the virtues of him who has known (the Lord), the Soul of all. I, the poet Kal, sing the fair praise of Guru Nanak, who has enjoyed Raj and Jog. ॥4॥
Kapil: the sage of the Sankhya school. Parasram, son of the sage Jamdagan, was a warrior with an axe, whose might Shri Ram took from him. Udho, Akrur and Bidar were devotees of Krishna.
1390.1: The four castes and the six orders of ascetics sing his virtues; Brahma and the others dwell on his virtues. Shesh Nag of the thousand tongues sings his virtues with relish, his attention fixed in one unbroken strain from first to last. Mahadev (Shiva), the renunciant, sings the virtues of him who has known (the Lord) in unbroken meditation. I, the poet Kal, sing the fair praise of Guru Nanak, who has enjoyed Raj and Jog. ॥5॥
The six orders: yogis, Jangams, sannyasis and the other three orders of Indian ascetics.
1390.2: He has enjoyed Raj and Jog; the One without enmity dwells within his heart. The whole creation has been saved; holding to the Name without a break, he has crossed over. Sanak and the others from the beginning, and Janak and the others through the ages, sing his virtues. Blessed, blessed is the Guru; blessed is his birth in the world, fruitful and good. Even in the cities of the nether world resounds the cry of (your) victory: so the humble poet Kal has declared; O Guru Nanak, lover of the relish of the Lord's Name, you have enjoyed Raj and Jog. ॥6॥
1390.3: In the Satjug you enjoyed (Raj and Jog); the form of Vaman (the dwarf) pleased you, and you deceived Bali. In the Treta you enjoyed (them), and were called Ram, of Raghu's line. In the Duapar (you were) Krishna Murari; (slaying) Kans, you set him free, gave the kingdom to Ugrasain, and fearlessness to your devotees. In the Kalyug, approved (by the Lord), you were called Nanak, Guru Angad and Amar (Das). The revered Guru's rule is unmoving and unshakable: so the Primal Being has commanded. ॥7॥

Satjug, Treta and Duapar: the first three of the four ages of the Puranas. Vaman, Vishnu's dwarf incarnation, deceived King Bali. Kans, the tyrant king of Mathura, was Krishna's uncle; slaying him, Krishna gave the kingdom back to his father Ugrasain.
1390.4: Ravidas the devotee sings his virtues, (and) Jaidev and Trilochan; Nama the devotee and Kabir ever sing of him, whose eyes look on all alike. Beni the devotee tells the virtues of him who, in Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise), enjoys the joy of the spirit, and who, through the meditation of yoga and the Guru's wisdom, knows none but God. Sukhdev and Parikhat tell his virtues; Gotam the sage has sung his praise. O poet Kal, the fair praise of Guru Nanak, ever new, has spread over the world. ॥8॥

Ravidas, Jaidev, Trilochan, Nama (Namdev), Kabir and Beni are Bhagats whose bani is in Sri Guru Granth Sahib. Sukhdev, the son of the sage Vyas, recited the Bhagavat Purana to King Parikhat. Gotam: the sage of the Nyaya school.
1390.5: In the nether world the serpent devotees, the Nag and the others, sing his virtues. Mahadev ever tells his virtues, and the yogis, the celibates and the Jangams too. The sage Vyas sings his virtues, he who has pondered the Vedas and their grammar. Brahma tells his virtues, he who by (the Lord's) Hukam fashioned all creation. (Guru Nanak) has known Brahm, who fills the universes and their regions, to be the same with attributes and without. O Kal, repeat the fair praise of Guru Nanak, who has enjoyed Sahaj and Jog. ॥9॥
1390.6: The nine Naths sing his virtues: blessed is the Guru, merged in the True One. Mandhata tells his virtues, he who was called a chakravarti (a king over all the earth). King Bali, dwelling in the seventh nether world, sings his virtues. Bharthari, who stays with his guru, ever tells his virtues. Durbasa, King Puru and Angra have sung the praise of Guru Nanak. O poet Kal, the fair praise of Guru Nanak abides, of itself, in every heart. ॥10॥

The nine Naths: the perfected masters of the yogis, such as Gorakhnath. Mandhata and Puru are kings of the Puranas; Bharthari was a famous yogi of Gorakhnath's order, by tradition a king of Ujjain who gave up his throne for yoga; Durbasa and Angra are sages of the Puranas.
